settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: XmlFactory exposes setXMLInputFactory (lines 340-351) and constructors taking an XMLInputFactory (lines 90-96), so callers can supply a pre-hardened factory, shifting responsibility away from this module.

pom.xml declares Woodstox (com.fasterxml.woodstox:woodstox-core, lines 89-94) which in normal deployments replaces the JDK StAX provider and has different (generally more restrictive) entity defaults; the dependency here is test-scoped, so behavior depends on the consuming application's classpath.
Only IS_COALESCING is explicitly forced; no explicit enabling of DTD or external entities was found in source, so the gap is an omission rather than an intentional activation.
No README or configuration documentation in the reviewed files instructs users about entity hardening, but also no source path was found that enables insecure DTD features.
candidates.description: XmlFactory, when no XMLInputFactory is supplied, builds one via XMLInputFactory.newInstance() (XmlFactory.java:112-114) and the only parser property configured is IS_COALESCING=true inside _initFactories (XmlFactory.java:136-142). Properties that block external entity / DTD resolution (e.g. XMLInputFactory.SUPPORT_DTD=false / IS_SUPPORTING_EXTERNAL_ENTITIES=false, or the "javax.xml.stream.isSupportingExternalEntities" property) are never set, nor is secure-processing requested. Most FromXmlParser input paths (InputStream/Reader/byte[]/char[] and the XMLStreamReader overloads in XmlFactory._createParser / createParser, lines 486-604) feed attacker-controlled XML directly into this factory-created reader. With a StAX provider whose defaults enable DTD/external entities (notably the JDK SJSXP provider selected by XMLInputFactory.newInstance() when Woodstox is absent), a crafted document containing a DOCTYPE with external entities can cause the underlying parser to resolve external resources while this module merely streams tokens, which is the classic XXE exposure for XML data-binding libraries. This is reported as a configuration/hardening candidate because reachability and effect hinge on which StAX provider is on the runtime classpath and on whether the caller injects a hardened XMLInputFactory.
missing_evidence: Actual runtime StAX provider in a deployment and its default values for SUPPORT_DTD / IS_SUPPORTING_EXTERNAL_ENTITIES / secure-processing.

A concrete call path in application code or tests exercising parsing of an untrusted document with a DOCTYPE through the default factory (no test in the reviewed tree demonstrates external entity resolution).
Verification (via build/run) that the default provider actually resolves external entities under this version; could not be executed with read-only tools.
preconditions: Application parses untrusted XML through XmlMapper/XmlFactory without supplying its own hardened XMLInputFactory.
Runtime StAX provider selected by XMLInputFactory.newInstance() has DTD/external-entity support enabled by default (e.g. JDK SJSXP when Woodstox is not present).
Attacker can supply XML content containing a DOCTYPE with external entity declarations.
candidates.title: Default StAX XMLInputFactory is created without disabling DTD/external-entity processing (XXE hardening gap)
